goal: Find an odd composite n = f1*f2 that is a strong base-2 pseudoprime AND a strong Lucas pseudoprime with Selfridge Method A parameters (a Baillie-PSW pseudoprime).

derivation: Lemma 2 follows from Lemma 1 (exact criterion, proved & checked). Pools = primes p=2x+1 with x,x+1 z-smooth (CHM closure), 5 not | x(x+1); optimized A/B/excluded partition by annealing, tracing Pareto frontier of (log2|G|, N).
falsification_test: z=100 (13,340 pairs; 804 inert primes) and z=150 (73,726 pairs) frontiers for the three largest 2-adic classes, using true orders ord_p2 and z(p).
lemma: Lemma 2: if all p in S are inert for D=5, share one 2-adic class (v2 ord_p2, v2 z(p)), odd(ord_p 2)|L1, odd(z(p))|L2, gcd(L1,L2)=1, |S| odd and prod S = 1 mod L1, = -1 mod L2, then prod S is a BPSW psp. Question: is there a pool P with 2^|P| >= |G|=phi(L1)phi(L2)*2 at a group size where subset-product search is feasible (log2|G| <= ~300)?
mechanism: Pomerance subset-product construction (Williams-type numbers), strong version, D=5
next_transformation: Test D=-7 (Q=2) variant which frees prime 5; then global review (likely STOP for constructive search).
outcome: Best: z=100 class (2,0): N=16 at log2|G|=126 (expected solutions 2^-110); z=150 class (2,0): N=30 at log2|G|=272 (2^-242); F2 class (1,2): N=24 at 230 bits. N/log2|G| stays ~0.11-0.13. Weak-version literature (Chen-Greene 2003) crosses N=log2|G| only near 1240-1840 bits, where Wagner-type search costs >= 2^80. Route infeasible at searchable scales.

next_transformation: Close D-variation; test parametric (Chernick-type) family route.
outcome: Criterion verified. Raw pool ~2x, optimised frontier ratio still ~0.1 (z=150: N=17 at 174.5 bits). No improvement.

derivation: Monotonicity at r*=max root of f_j-1 forces common root; then n+1 = C prod(u+2/a_j) vs n = C prod(u+1/a_j) gives sum 1/a_j = 0.
falsification_test: Proof checked by hand; k=3 general case also solved directly earlier (only degenerate f_2=f_1).
lemma: No k>=2 distinct linear f_j in Q[t] (same-sign slopes) with f_j-1 | n-1 and f_j+1 | n+1, n=prod f_j.
mechanism: Constructive parametrization: polynomial (Chernick-type) families of Williams-type numbers
outcome: PROVED for linear families (and compositions g_j(h(t))). Higher degree not settled.

evidence: Exact criterion (Lemma 1) proved+checked; strong-version Pomerance pools measured at z=100,150 for D=5 and D=-7: best N/log2|G| ~ 0.1 (e.g. 30 primes vs 272 bits); linear polynomial families proved impossible (Lemma 3); two-factor, small-order and Q=2 coupling routes heuristically negligible.
global_reason: Remaining options are either infeasible compute (>=2^80, or extending exhaustive search past 1e21) or low-information (higher-degree polynomial families, more overdetermined than the linear case already excluded).
next_discriminating_action: Stop constructive search. A genuinely new idea is needed: a polynomial-time algorithm for high-density subset products in groops with odd-order components, or a non-Williams mechanism making ord_p(2) and z(p) small together.
theory_of_success: Only known mechanism (Pomerance/Williams-type subset products) needs groups >= ~2^1200-2^2500 before solutions are expected, and searching them costs >= 2^80 with Wagner-type methods; no structural shortcut found (odd-order components block linear algebra).
